texts: On day 75 of Year 1, a sky-cat hunted nightmoths at the Sunken Cove on a clear night.
Sky-cats rarely hunt at the Sunken Cove.
The Council discussed burning wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern.
Wintergloss repels nightmoths from a lantern.
The Council declined the wintergloss, because the Stilllight Lantern drew a handful of nightmoths.

q1_issues.issue: "Wintergloss repels nightmoths from a lantern" is a verbal generic with bare kind-denoting NPs on both sides, yet it is emitted as a flat top-level event with the kind symbols wintergloss and nightmoth filling Agent/Theme, rather than the kind-level relation or the distributing Implication rule the instruction set mandates for a generic over a kind.

Genericity is expressed by lowering each separate role atom to (STV 0.9 0.9), which is not a licensed use of the confidence/strength dial — the dial grades kind-level claims and rules, not the individual role atoms of one reified event.

The indefinite "a lantern" in the Source oblique is rendered as the bare constant lantern instead of a fresh witness plus its (Member ... lantern) atom, contrary to the rule that an oblique's object NP follows ordinary NP rules (an article mints a witness).

q2_gaps: a gerund complement of a verb that is neither a control verb, a finite-that-clause attitude verb, a perception verb nor a causative ("The Council discussed burning wintergloss") — no routing is specified, so occurrence-neutrality of the complement event rests only on analogy to the control-verb pattern

an indefinite temporal NP carrying an adjectival modifier ("on a clear night") — day-parts are bare Time symbols and calendar expressions are structured terms, with no licensed slot for a modifier and no licensed witness filler for the Time role
a day-of-year ordinal calendar ("day 75 of Year 1") — (Day n) is defined as the day-of-month granularity term, so (Day 75) beside (Year 1) has no stated reading

a two-bare-kind relational generic that also carries an oblique ("repels nightmoths from a lantern") — the kind-level relation has no slot for the third argument, and only the analogous adjectivally-restricted-subject case is addressed
review.notes: Sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 track the instruction set closely (compound genus atoms, the rarely-rule with its QuantifierPhrase companion, the capitalized-common-noun "the Council" with no Name, CardinalityPhrase for "a handful", Because with the main clause first). The one clear routing defect is sentence 4's generic.

issues.reason: Both arguments of 'Wintergloss repels nightmoths' are bare kind-denoting NPs (mass subject, bare-plural object), which is the stated trigger for the kind-level relation (Repel wintergloss nightmoth); reifying a flat event with the kind symbols in Agent/Theme is precisely the routing the relational-generic rule forbids ('not a per-instance rule', and the two forms 'are not comparable').

The dial is for generalizations only — 'Individual facts keep 0.99' — so (STV 0.9 0.9) on each separate role atom of one reified event witness grades role assignments the sentence states flatly, a placement the instruction set licenses nowhere (a generic's 0.9/0.9 rides the single kind-level atom or the Implication).

The oblique rule states that 'the oblique's object NP follows the ordinary NP rules (an article mints a witness with its kind atom; a bare mass / domain / proper name stays a constant)', and 'a lantern' carries an article, so the bare constant lantern with no typing atom anywhere in the parse violates it.

gaps_confirmed: a gerund complement of a verb that is neither a control verb, a finite-that-clause attitude verb, a perception verb nor a causative ('discussed burning wintergloss') — no routing is stated, so occurrence-neutrality rests on analogy to the control-verb pattern

an indefinite, adjectivally modified temporal NP ('on a clear night') — day-parts are bare Time symbols and calendar expressions are structured terms, with no licensed modifier slot and no licensed witness filler for Time
a day-of-year ordinal calendar ('day 75 of Year 1') — (Day n) is exemplified only as the day-of-month granularity beside a (Month ...), so (Day 75) with (Year 1) has no stated reading

a two-bare-kind relational generic that also carries an oblique ('repels nightmoths from a lantern') — the kind-level relation has exactly two slots, and the escape to the distributing rule is licensed only for an adjectivally-restricted subject
new_gaps: definite anaphora to a bare mass constant ('burning wintergloss' ... 'declined the wintergloss'): the reserve rule bars the bare class symbol 'for a specific definite individual' while the anaphoric-definite rule mandates reusing the antecedent symbol, and nothing states how a specific portion of a previously-mentioned mass is encoded — minting sk_wintergloss_1 would sever the link to the s3 constant
adjudication.defect_summary: Sentence 4's compliant form is the single kind-level relation (: s4_repel (Repel wintergloss nightmoth) (STV 0.9 0.9)), not a reified event with kinds in role slots. That one atom is also the only place the empirical-generic 0.9/0.9 belongs; role atoms of an event witness are individual facts and keep 1.0/0.99 or do not exist. For 'from a lantern' NO compliant form is licensed — the kind-level relation has only two slots and the distributing-rule fallback is licensed only for an adjectivally-restricted subject — so the oblique must be dropped and the loss recorded as a gap, which is why the reviewer's witness remedy would be moot under the correct routing.
adjudication.notes: Sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 are faithful: the sky_cat/nightmoth genus atoms, the strength-0.1 'rarely' rule with its QuantifierPhrase companion, 'the Council' as a Name-less capitalized common noun, the episodic bare-plural group witnesses, CardinalityPhrase for 'a handful', and (Because sk_decline_1 sk_draw_1) main-clause-first. The gap-territory improvisations — (Time sk_hunt_1 sk_night_1) for 'a clear night', (Day 75)/(Year 1), and the tenseless sk_burn_1 under discuss — emit nothing false or ill-typed and stand.
